commenti.body: I don't see how a list of events that happen in the film and an account of how you would have acted instead constitutes a critique. It's a movie about idealism vs reality in the education system and the path to hell being paved with good intentions, you can't just say LOL why didn't they just expel everyone

Having a list of things that should have happened doesn't constitute a valid criticism of film neither does it bring any points of discussion to the film.


>Obi wan should have killed darth vader as soon as he could, therefore it's a bad film, the hobbits should have flown to mount doom, therefore it's a bad story.

In europe especially, people act like this. There is a strong incentive not to offend and treat every service user as a customer. In hospitals, schools, government facilities, even prisons - the story this film tells is all to similar to situations in these kind of establishments.


I hate to break the news, but as you get older you realise adults very very rarely act like adults - no matter how high up or educated, we are all just stumbling through life and treating things as they come, using as much past experience as possible to guide us. When we come across situations a little more complicated - there are so many factors you must take into account and when every other person around you is trying to resolve the issue in their own way you are left to your own devices. This film tells the story of that and how the naivety of the teacher really doesn't do anything but isolate her more and worsen the situation.  


The film would be different if it happened in a different country but i believe the issues wouldn't be resolved any better. Someone will always get hurt and another will always feel like they didn't do all they possibly could.

the review is directed towards storytelling mechanisms that lack verisimilitude. A plot that needs so many questionable events to create movement is just poor writing. 

Our protagonist has principles but lacks the ability of adapting, the stubborness she shows reveals a lack of ability of adapting to circumstances up to a point where it feels like she's not a functioning human. And if the movie wanted to present a character with this problematic, it'd be interesting, but the problem is that they offer her story without noticing this fact. So it just feels dumb. 

Adults can have a hard time growing, of course, and act childlish and irrational. But a drama in which the characters act like puppets without depth or purpose, and there's no sign of them of searching sense, no arc whatsoever, isn't appealing at all for my taste, 

  
The ending, where (spoiler) the kid suddenly shows the rubik cube and a happy chord is heard and the film wants to tell us that inexplicably he now is no longer angry at her is the cheapest thing I've seen in a long time. And then they show us how he triumphantly gets out of the school sitting in his throne. I don't think there's any meaning there, just common places and cliches without any sort of direction. It's a cheap telefilm to fill saturday afternoon tv.

The protagonist is acting irrational because teachers get hardly any support. Which is an accurate depiction, especially the dealing with kid's parents. That said, I don't know why this movie got an Oscar nomination. It does not stand out in any way.

the meeting with the parents felt specially false for me, as she didn't took part in the accusations or the methods, actually she opposed them. The whole method of trying to catch the thieves was strange and unrealistic and ineffective, just effectist
Questionable events? May you explain yourself better? Because right now i read Your post as a rant with no real critisism

Starting with the way they decide to catch the thief, then her plan to catch the thief, then there's the accused reaction, the kids reaction, the parents reaction, then the press, the board, and the ending that resolves nothing... So yeah, actually the whole plot: sorry, but that's not how the world works. 


It's an insubstantial screenplay, without much to say without notion of what storytelling devices are.

Your quote starts out clarifying that the problem is society, not the movie. Depicting flaws in society shouldn’t be easy to watch. If the movie makes you frustrated, that’s a good thing! 

I’ve read from German reviewers that the movie is accurate to their experiences. I’m from America and I wouldn’t expect a viewer in Germany to 100% relate to American movies. Why should I 100% relate to German movies? 

I honestly like not relating to foreign movies because then I can look up whether something I noticed is true or not.
